draft.title: Types of aid
card: aid given directly from one government to another, such as Australia funding a health program run with the government of Fiji.
aid that governments pay into a larger body, which then decides how to spend it. Examples are the United Nations (UN) and the World Bank.
groups that are not part of any government, such as charities. They raise money from the public and other sources to give aid.
Aid can be humanitarian or development. Humanitarian aid meets urgent needs after a disaster or conflict. Development aid builds long-term health and wellbeing.
draft.remember: Who gives and how it is passed on sorts aid into bilateral, multilateral or non-government.

a.q: Several governments pay money into a UN agency, which then chooses where to spend it. What type of aid is this?
a.why: The money is pooled in a larger body that decides how to use it, which is multilateral aid. It is not bilateral, because bilateral aid goes straight from one government to another.
a.clue: Who decides where the pooled money goes?

b.q: After a cyclone, a charity in Brisbane uses public donations to send food and clean water to a village in Vanuatu. How is this aid best described?
b.why: A charity is not part of a government, and the aid meets urgent needs after a disaster, so it is humanitarian. It is not bilateral, because no government is giving directly to another government.
b.clue: Who is giving, and is the need urgent or long-term?
